Explore our capabilities

RBC Clear

Global Investment Banking

Cross-border advisory and financing capabilities with industry-specific expertise, supporting clients across M&A, capital raising and strategic transactions.

Learn more

Corporate Banking

Corporate and institutional lending capabilities across the credit spectrum, supporting clients with acquisition financing, revolving and term loans, letters of credit and other tailored credit solutions.

Global Markets

A new
standard formulti-asset
electronic trading.

Trading desks are evolving, and the gap between real-time intelligence and multi-asset execution is closing fast.

MAAS is our execution platform. It works hand in hand with MATA, our analytics platform — together, two complementary capabilities that connect pre-trade intelligence to disciplined execution across all major asset classes and index events.

Because in complex markets, the traders who win aren't just faster - they're better informed, better connected, and better positioned to execute.

See MAAS in action

Skin: rbccm-two-up-cards--features.xsl MAAS+MATA parity. Dark section, one --dark card + one --light card, 5-slot bullet list per card.

TWO PLATFORMS, ONE CONNECTED WORKFLOW

Better insight for stronger execution

MATA - Analytics

Transform data into trading intelligence

Turn cross-asset insight into actionable pre-trade intelligence, helping you evaluate execution decisions before you move.

  • Quantify expected execution costs before commitment
  • Compare strategies side by side to evaluate potential outcomes
  • Explore interactive outlier views to focus on higher-risk or harder-to-trade orders
  • Monitor market conditions and portfolio exposures
  • Model scenarios across asset classes
MAAS - Execution

Drive stronger performance outcomes

Turn trading insight into disciplined execution, with advanced technology designed to adapt as market conditions change.

  • Access adaptive algorithms built for live market conditions
  • Select AI-powered strategies tailored to execution objectives
  • Route orders intelligently to help minimize market impact
  • Support consistency across asset classes through shared execution logic, connected workflows and platform-wide controls
  • Benchmark performance against pre-trade expectations
  • Trade equities, futures, currencies and rates from a single execution framework

Variant -- data-animate (fires when scrolled into view)
Scroll down ↓

Eyebrow · fadeInUp · 0ms

Heading · fadeInUp · 120ms

Body · fadeInUp · 240ms. Each element starts hidden and plays once when it enters the viewport. The eyebrow / heading / description cascade is the pattern every section uses.

Variant -- data-stagger-parent (children play in sequence)
Scroll down ↓

Parent: data-stagger-parent="fadeInUp" data-stagger-step="150". Children need no attributes.

Card 10ms
Card 2150ms
Card 3300ms
Card 4450ms
Variant -- other animate.css effects
Scroll down ↓

Any animate.css name works in data-animate. These are the ones worth reaching for.

fadeIndata-animate="fadeIn"
fadeInUpthe default
fadeInDowneyebrows, heroes
zoomInuse sparingly
fadeInLeftsplit layouts
fadeInRightsplit layouts
slideInUpno fade
flipInXprobably don't
Variant -- data-animate-duration / data-animate-delay

        Meet the host

        Valerie Grimba

        Director, Global ETF Strategy, RBC Capital Markets

        Valerie runs the Global ETF Strategy team at RBC Capital Markets, helping institutional clients understand and implement ETF strategies and bridging the gap between clients and ETF trade execution. She sits at the center of a desk that serves as designated broker to roughly 300 ETF mandates and acts as authorized participant across more than 90% of the Canadian ETF market — working with everyone from the largest pension funds to family offices.

        With over 15 years of global institutional sales and trading experience, Valerie’s career has spanned trading floors across Canada, the U.S. and Australasia, including roles at Bear Stearns, CIBC World Markets and Macquarie before joining RBC.

        S&E Notes

        Timely, short-form commentary from our economists and strategists.

        Economics

        Frances Donald | Aug 12, 2026

        BoC Rate Decision Preview

        Inflation tick-up reduces probability of a 50bps cut next week; 25bps remains baseline.

        Headline CPI came in two tenths above consensus, and the trimmed-mean measures the Bank watches most closely stopped decelerating for the first time since March. That is not, on its own, an argument against easing.

        Financial conditions have loosened materially since the spring. Our baseline: 25bps next week, 25bps in the following meeting, and a terminal rate of 2.25% by mid-2026.

        Read more

        Geopolitics

        Helima Croft | Aug 28, 2026

        Iran conflict: six-month update

        Diplomatic resolution remains elusive; markets modestly pricing in a sustained Strait of Hormuz premium.

        As the Iran conflict reaches its six-month mark, diplomatic resolution remains elusive despite repeated market optimism about swift resolution. Energy markets have partially normalized but structural risk persists.

        Our base case: modest crude premium through year-end, with tail risk on any escalation into shipping lanes. Strategic petroleum reserves remain the swing factor.

        Read more

        Equity Markets

        Lori Calvasina | Sep 2, 2026

        S&P 500 target refresh

        Lifting our year-end target on stronger earnings breadth; still constructive but tail risks widen.

        Earnings breadth has broadened noticeably in Q2, with 60%+ of S&P 500 constituents beating on both revenue and EPS. That's the strongest breadth since late 2023.

        Read more
